answer: Each agent must escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work, and a randomly selected peer quorum releases payment only after independently checking the result. A Sybil operator can wander through many identities, but each one locks capital and must recruit credible reviewers; copied identities do not multiply the stake. The tide of fake submissions therefore raises the attacker’s funding and coordination costs, while a lantern-like audit sample can slash stakes when reviewers collude or approve invalid work.
